substantive_relations.relationship: Defines social facts through externality and constraining force, rather than mere prevalence among individuals.
substantive_relations.note: Own chapter I opening read, including obligations, conventions and currents. His examples are attributed illustrations, not independently tested universal laws.

substantive_relations.relationship: Separates the causal explanation of institutions from their utility or present functions.
substantive_relations.note: Own chapter V section I opening read; changed uses and institutional survivals challenge explanation by usefulness alone. This is a methodological resource, without claiming every comparative historian accepted it.

limits: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.
